title: Cross-signal Quantized Shadow Failure Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes an end-to-end triage and mitigation workflow for regressions that appear only (or primarily) when models are served with quantized artifacts during shadow/dark deployments. The emphasis is on cross-signal correlation: combining telemetry from runtime, eval-harness probe traces, prompt-set fingerprints, and quantization profile indicators to rapidly identify root cause, apply temporary mitigations, and produce a corrective plan.

Scope:
- Applies to regressions observed in Dedicated, Private, or Hosted shadow lanes where a quantized model artifact is in the serving path.
- Covers detection, triage, temporary mitigations, rollback/rollforward patterns, and postmortem actions.
- Out of scope: non-quantization runtime hardware faults (GPU ECC faults, node-level networking issues) unless correlated with quant artifacts.

Why this playbook exists:
- Quantized artifacts reduce inference cost but introduce subtle distributional distortions (token-level probabilities, attention weight perturbations) that only manifest on certain prompt families or long-context interactions.
- Shadow lanes produce limited traffic and may miss rare prompts; therefore we rely on targeted probes and telemetry to amplify signal.

Signals to collect (ordered by diagnostic value):
1) Response Stability Index (RSI) change per probe slice — earliest semantic signal from eval-harness.
2) Token-level log-prob delta distribution (baseline vs quant) — shows where quantization changed model scoring.
3) KV-cache divergence metrics (cache_hit_mismatch_percent) — indicates attention/key-value precision issues.
4) Latency and tail-p90/p99 jitter (quantizable kernels sometimes increase micro-tail variance).
5) Prompt fingerprint hit-rate (prompt-set signature match) — identifies affected families.
6) Embedding cosine drift for anchor prompts (if embeddings used for retrieval/contexts).
7) Error rates and downstream reranker flips for multi-stage pipelines.

Initial detection (automated alert triggers):
- Alert: RSI-drop-large (threshold: RSI decrease >= 0.12 over 1h for a slice with >= 50 probes) -> page oncall eval-eng.
- Alert: Quant-token-shift-high (KL divergence of token-prob distributions > 0.06 against baseline for top-1 tokens) -> notify quant-team + runtime.
- Alert: KV-cache-divergence > 2% for requests with context length > 2048 -> notify serving-runtime.

First-response checklist (oncall):
1) Confirm signal: open the probe dashboard and validate that the RSI drop is reproducible across the last 3 probe snapshots.
2) Identify scope: use prompt fingerprint table to compute top 3 affected slices and their traffic share.
3) Correlate runtime metrics: check shadow-runner logs for quantizer-service warnings and any kernel fallback events.
4) Validate artifact: find the quantized model artifact id (artifact: model-name@quant-variant-<hash>) and compare with last-known-good artifact.
5) Capture artifacts: save the following to the incident folder: probe-snapshots (JSON), token-prob diffs (CSV), and example requests that show divergence (redact PII).

Diagnostic steps (detailed):
Step A — Reproduce with eval harness in isolated environment:
- Run targeted probe set (top 500 matching prompts from affected slices) against both artifacts: baseline_fp (float32) and suspect_quant. Use the quantized-replay-orchestrator in shadow mode.
- Collect: full token-level trace, attention norms, KV-cache sizes, and response generation timestamps.
- Command example:
  ./orchestrator replay --suite=affected-slice-2026 --baseline=model-main-fp32 --candidate=model-main-q4_0 --output=./replay-output.json

Step B — Diff analysis and heuristics:
- Compute token-delta heatmap (per-position average delta in top-5 log-probs).
- Compute attention-norm-shift: compare mean L2 norm of attention between baseline and quant at each layer.
- If attention-norm-shift > 0.08 at any layer for >10% of prompts, mark as attention-suspect.

Step C — Narrow to prompt families and context patterns:
- For affected sample requests, extract prompt templates and variable slots; group by template fingerprint.
- Check whether long-prefix context (> 2048 tokens) correlates with higher divergence.

Mitigation matrix (temporary, ordered by risk):
1) Shadow lane throttling: reduce traffic to suspect quant lane by 80% while maintaining 10% for monitoring. (Low risk, rapid)
2) Transparent rollforward to a different quant-profile (e.g., q4_0 -> q4_1-with-dp) that is known to preserve attention scaling. (Medium risk)
3) Fallback to float artifact for user-facing lanes (if SLA dictates). (High cost, high assurance)
4) Prompt rewrite shim: for known templates, add stabilizing priming tokens or truncate long context adaptively per prompt fingerprint. (Workload-specific)

Rollback and rollout guidance:
- Fast rollback: use the platform's artifact-switch API with version pins and observability gating. Rollback plan must include: change id, operator, expected impact, and post-rollback smoke probes.
- Canary rollforward: deploy candidate quant-profile to 5% of traffic with probe gating for 1h, then 25% for 3h, then 100% if metrics stable.
- Safety gates (required): RSI >= baseline - 0.04, KL_token <= 0.02, KV-cache-divergence <= 0.5%. If any gate fails, automated rollback to previous stable variant.

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: applied-ml (oncall: eval-eng).
- Secondary owner: serving-runtime oncall.
- Quantization SME: quant-team@redwood (pager).
- Channel: #inc-quant-shadow (Slack), create incident in Incident Manager (owner: primary).

Postmortem and corrective actions checklist:
1) Root cause hypothesis validated with replay diffs and attention analysis.
2) If quantization rounding model is implicated: schedule quant-profile re-tune with per-layer scale calibration and retrain activation scaling tables.
3) Add targeted probes to the eval-harness for discovered prompt templates and long-context patterns.
4) Update quant-profile manifest with known-unsafe prompt fingerprints and add an auto-fallback rule.
5) Document changes in model-onboarding: add a new artifact test that includes the failing probe family.

Example queries and artifacts to attach (copy these into incident folder):
- SQL: top affected templates by RSI:
  SELECT template_id, COUNT(*) AS hits, AVG(rsi_delta) AS avg_rsi FROM probe_results WHERE artifact_id = 'model-main-q4_0' GROUP BY template_id ORDER BY avg_rsi ASC LIMIT 20;
- Token-diff command (python snippet):
  python tools/token_diff.py --baseline ./baseline_traces.json --candidate ./quant_traces.json --out token_diff.csv

Configuration table (examples):
| Setting | Recommended value | Rationale | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| RSI-alert-threshold | 0.12 | Sensitive but reduces false-positives for rare slices | eval-eng |
| KL-token-alert | 0.06 | Highlights token-level reordering | quant-team |
| Probe-sampling-rate | 1% production, 100% shadow | Preserve production costs; amplify in shadow | eval-harness |
| Shadow-traffic-cap | 5% | Limits cost and blast radius | platform |

Operational notes and gotchas:
- Quantization issues often amplify for templates that rely on exact enumeration (lists, code, citations). Look for tokenization boundary shifts.
- Mixed-precision kernel fallbacks may mask error modes; ensure kernel-fallback logs are not suppressed by noise filters.
- Privacy: redact PII from captured request samples before sharing outside primary owners.

Related artifacts and playbooks:
- Quantized replay orchestrator spec (see related_pages).
- Model promotion safety contract for quant profiles (add as related page after update).

Appendix: Example incident timeline (short):
- 00:00: RSI-drop-large alert triggers, eval-eng paged.
- 00:20: First-response checklist completed, affected template identified (help-center-auto-summarize).
- 00:40: Repro replay shows token-shift at positions 12-18 for 72% of samples; attention-norm shift at layer 10.
- 01:15: Temporary mitigation: throttle shadow lane and enable q4_1 candidate at 5%.
- 04:00: Gate metrics stable on q4_1; schedule quant-profile re-tune and create postmortem.

Contact matrix:
- eval-eng oncall: eval-oncall@redwood.internal
- serving-runtime oncall: runtime-oncall@redwood.internal
- quant-team lead: aria.patel@redwood.com

Document maintenance:
- Owner (this doc): Maya Chen (applied-ml). Review cadence: quarterly or after any quantation-led incident.
- Add newly discovered prompt templates to the probe registry and link to the model-onboarding artifact entry for future promotions.
